note: Re-judged on 2026-09-20 by an independent reader, after Negotiate's signature moved from (local, remote []Capability, localASN, peerASN uint32) to (local, remote []Capability, identity PeerIdentity). Inside each unit named here the change is one line, the call shape, and every assertion is byte-identical (git diff HEAD over internal/core/bgp/capability/negotiated_test.go). The new shape cannot move what these cases prove: Negotiate reads identity only where it stores LocalASN and PeerASN on the Negotiated, and where buildSubComponents copies the struct into n.Identity. No branch in Negotiate, and none in negotiatePathsLimitDirection, reads Internal or either AS number, so the iBGP verdict the struct now carries has no path to the PATHS-LIMIT maps. The identity each call passes is self-consistent too: 65001 against 65002 with Internal left false is an external session, which is what the two positional AS numbers meant before. Section 3: "The PATHS-LIMIT capability MUST be ignored if the ADD-PATH capability is not present." TestNegotiatePathsLimit is the positive: ADD-PATH both-mode for ipv4/unicast on both sides, and the two directions are pinned on exact, distinct values, the remote's 10 in PathsLimitSend and the local's 5 in PathsLimitRecv, so a direction swap and a floor reading each fail it. TestNegotiatePathsLimitNoAddPath is the negative: the same two PATHS-LIMIT capabilities with no ADD-PATH on either side, and both maps must stay at zero. The producing branch is "n.addPath[f]&direction == 0" in negotiatePathsLimitDirection (internal/core/bgp/capability/negotiated.go); remove it and the negative reads 10 and 5, so the assertion discriminates. The negative buffer holds Multiprotocol and PathsLimit only, so no neighbouring rule decides it. Ze is stricter than the sentence, because it requires the negotiated DIRECTION and not the bare presence of ADD-PATH. A limit on paths the session will never carry changes nothing on the wire, so the stricter reading implements the requirement rather than falling short of it. No discrimination record: both tags predate HEAD and the gate grandfathers them. 2026-09-26 RE-AUDIT, stale-requirement: the checklist line lost its quotation marks and gained the sentence's full stop, so it is now a verbatim span of Section 3 of rfc/drafts/draft-abraitis-idr-addpath-paths-limit.txt. The obligation is the sentence this note already quotes, and the tagged units are byte-identical (TestNegotiatePathsLimitNoAddPath re-read this pass: both PATHS-LIMIT maps must stay zero with no ADD-PATH). Verdict unchanged.
